verified.coverageNote: 27851 distinct JDK Double.parseDouble inputs compare exact canonical bits or rejection in 218 whitebox groups, with 346 new strings and three additional groups. New long tails and midpoint extensions exercise conclusive/ambiguous prefix intervals. Existing 24254 primitive rendering patterns still pass. Public Config accessor/render suites are freshly compared live; fourteen saved-native suites replay 30550 runs with historical overlap counts retained. This is not exhaustive conformance.
verified.api: Direct UTF-16 numeric trim/sign/suffix and ASCII integer scans avoid character-array allocation while preserving Unicode fallback, original NaN handling, diagnostic text and the input-length bound. Tiny coefficients use exact 32-/768-digit prefix intervals and return only for identical rounded endpoints; ambiguous long inputs retain runtime conversion.

performance.scope: Ten exact-render workloads, sixteen existing workloads and three retained Double-list reads compare current, fixed 0.17 and native Config. Long coefficients exercise conclusive prefix intervals and unresolved midpoint boundaries; the latter retain the full runtime conversion. Double-list output is compared as exact binary64 bit strings, converted after timing; public getDoubleList calls and list construction occur inside timing. Render timers retain the prepared ConfigValue; Java retains options and JS constructs its options object inside each call and include returned text; source parsing, optional partial resolution and final result-array serialization are excluded. The full baseline JS module dependency tree is loaded from the fixed Git commit. Retained workloads compare real Config methods with native Config; construction excluded, immutable operations/getter transport included, final result serialization excluded. Each workload has five fresh processes; Java legacy and retained workloads use separate processes. Startup, I/O and sustained/peak-memory parity are not measured.
